Feature flags select among backends: use_linux_sandbox_bwrap, use_legacy_landlock, experimental_windows_sandbox, elevated_windows_sandbox, windows_sandbox_service, prefer_mxc; config key windows.sandbox and windows.allow_mxc=false (opt-out). The MXC backend is a vendored git crate ('mxc') that calls an experimental CreateProcessInSandbox API on a BaseContainer-capable OS build and otherwise falls back to AppContainer; errors carry hints such as ERROR_ACCESS_DISABLED_BY_POLICY (1260) and 'contact your system administrator to allow the target executable to run in an MXC sandbox'. A helper executable codex-linux-sandbox exists for the Linux path. Spawn arguments seen: --sandbox-policy-cwd, --permission-profile, --windows-sandbox-level, --windows-sandbox-private-desktop-name, --use-legacy-landlock, --managed-network, --proxy-enforced, --deny-read-paths-json, --deny-write-paths-json.

name: Windows elevated sandbox: service, dedicated local accounts, WFP firewall filters, private desktop, DPAPI-protected credentials
what: On Windows the agent can run commands as separate low-privilege local users with network blocked at the firewall; setup needs one-time elevation, runs as a Windows service, and has a full uninstall that removes the accounts, profiles and rules.
how: A SYSTEM service (codex-windows-sandbox-service.exe, registered under HKLM SOFTWARE\OpenAI\Codex\WindowsSandboxService with a registered package family and runtime ownership record) provisions a local group CodexSandboxUsers and two accounts, CodexSandboxOnline and CodexSandboxOffline; the offline account's password is DPAPI-protected ('dpapi protect failed for offline user') and kept under CODEX_HOME .sandbox-secrets with setup_marker.json and setup_error.json beside it; setup serialises through the global mutex Global\CodexSandboxSetup. A persistent Windows Filtering Platform provider and sublayer ('Codex Windows Sandbox WFP') install filters named 'Codex Sandbox Offline - Block Non-Loopback Outbound', '...Block Non-Loopback Inbound', '...Block Loopback TCP (Except Proxy)', '...Block Loopback UDP', plus ICMP connect blocks; allowed proxy ports are passed in CODEX_WINDOWS_SANDBOX_PROXY_PORTS so only the managed proxy is reachable. Commands run on a private desktop (CodexSandboxDesktop-shared) so they cannot touch the interactive session. File access is done with ACLs: workspace-write adds per-writable-root capability SIDs, deny-read/deny-write path lists apply deny ACEs (the code refuses to apply a deny-read ACE to a filesystem root). An uninstall plan removes accounts, loaded profiles, the group and registered runtimes (PowerShell cleanup with event-log codes 3003/3004).

name: Command runner: restricted token, ConPTY, job objects and a spawn_request protocol
what: Every sandboxed Windows command is started by a small helper that applies a restricted token, wraps the process tree in a job object, attaches a pseudo console and receives its launch parameters over a private channel.
how: codex-command-runner.exe (windows-sandbox-rs/src/bin/command_runner/win.rs, process.rs, token.rs) uses CreateRestrictedToken, CreatePseudoConsole (ConPTY) and Job Objects (SetInformationJobObject); it fails if it is not given a parent-owned private desktop ('runner: missing parent-owned private desktop') and if a spawned ConPTY has no process job; it reads a spawn_request message ('runner: expected spawn_request') and passes launch payloads by environment variable (--launch-payload-env, payload must contain 1..N items). Unified exec uses the same runner for PTY sessions (windows-sandbox-rs/src/unified_exec/backends/legacy.rs).
verevonRelevance: Shows the minimum per-command isolation stack for a Windows agent (token, job, pty, desktop); relevant only if Verevon adds a Windows executor.
notes: Token restrictions (which SIDs and privileges are removed) were not decoded. Quality 4: Token, job and ConPTY stack is the expected minimum for Windows.

name: Shell environment policy and credential-broker-aware shell snapshots
what: The environment passed to agent commands is filtered by a declarative policy, and the runtime refuses to persist a shell snapshot that would contain a credential the proxy is meant to inject.
how: config shell_environment_policy {inherit, ignore_default_excludes, exclude, set, include_only, filters, experimental_use_profile} (ShellEnvironmentPolicyToml with 7 fields; mixing filters with legacy exclude or include_only is an error; duplicate filter names rejected); shell_snapshot feature captures the user's login-shell environment per shell (zsh, bash, PowerShell, cmd) inside its own sandbox (core/src/shell_snapshot.rs, shell_snapshot_sandbox.rs; messages 'shell snapshot contains a brokered credential outside exported environment', 'shell snapshot sandbox cannot be enforced on this host'); login_shell_package_path keeps bundled tools such as ripgrep on PATH when login-shell startup resets it; sandbox env keys TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP are redirected.
verevonRelevance: Verevon scrubs output (EC/scrub.rs) but not inbound environment; an allow/deny env filter plus snapshot refusal for brokered secrets is a small hardening step for process_start and code_interpreter.
